requirements.statement: Users can sign in securely so their tasks are private to them

criteria.must: An unauthenticated visitor is prompted to sign in before seeing any task data
After signing in, a user only sees tasks they created, never another user's tasks

requirements.statement: A user can create a task with a title

criteria.must: Submitting a new task with a title creates it and it appears in the user's task list
Submitting a new task with no title is rejected with a clear error

requirements.statement: A user can edit a task's title, tags, due date, or priority

criteria.must: Editing a task's title persists the new title
Editing a task's tags persists the new tag set
Editing a task's due date persists the new due date
Editing a task's priority persists the new priority

requirements.statement: A user can mark a task as complete

criteria.must: Marking a task complete changes its status to completed
A completed task no longer appears in the open task view

requirements.statement: A user can reopen a completed task

criteria.must: Reopening a completed task changes its status back to open
A reopened task appears again in the open task view

requirements.statement: A user can delete a task

criteria.must: Deleting a task removes it from the user's task list entirely

requirements.statement: A user can add tags to a task

criteria.must: A user can attach one or more tags to a task
A task's assigned tags are visible on the task

requirements.statement: A user can filter their tasks by tag

criteria.must: Filtering by a tag shows only tasks carrying that tag

requirements.statement: A user can set an optional due date on a task

criteria.must: A task can be created or edited with no due date
A task can be created or edited with a due date, and that date is shown on the task

requirements.statement: A user can sort or filter their tasks by due date

criteria.must: Sorting by due date orders tasks from soonest to latest due
Filtering by a due-date range shows only tasks whose due date falls within it

requirements.statement: A user can set a priority level (Low/Medium/High) on a task

criteria.must: A task can be created or edited with a priority of Low, Medium, or High
The task's priority is visible on the task

requirements.statement: A user can sort or filter their tasks by priority

criteria.must: Sorting by priority orders tasks from High to Low
Filtering by a priority level shows only tasks at that level

requirements.statement: A user sees a clear view of open (incomplete) tasks separate from completed ones

criteria.must: The default task view shows only open tasks
A separate view or section shows completed tasks and excludes open ones
